title: frameledger floor --json
description: The result of `frameledger floor FILE --fps N --json`: whether one run holds a frame-rate floor. A later release may add keys, and values to the open sets; a script ignores what it does not know. Print this file from the same frameledger that printed the result.

frameledger.description: The version of the frameledger that printed this.

summary.description: The opening sentences of the text output, in order. Wording may change in any release.

overrides.description: The --override flags given; empty for a command that takes none.

warnings.description: The warnings, each also a sentence in summary.

start_s.description: When the window starts, in seconds from the run's start.

frames.description: The frames ending inside the window.

fps.description: The older name of frames, holding the same count.

mean_ms.description: The window's mean frame/wall, in ms; null for a window with no frame.

pass.description: Whether the window meets the floor.

windows.description: Each whole one-second window judged; empty with --no-windows.

windows_skipped.description: The windows left out of the judging.

top_pass.description: category/name of the frame's largest depth-0 cpu or gpu cost; null when the frame has none.

slow_frames.description: The frames over the budget, slowest first.

frames_over_budget.description: How many judged frames are over the budget.

allowed.description: --allow-frames: how many frames may be over the budget.

rows_dropped.description: The close line's count of rows the writer dropped; null when the run has no close line.

finished.description: Whether the run has a close line.

generated_frames.description: How many of the run's frames a frame generator made.

result.description: The two checks. With the verdict error, a file could not be read and result holds no key.

floor_verdict.description: The verdict of floor: pass, fail, inconclusive when the run cannot settle it, or error when the file could not be read or breaks the format. A closed set.

floor_exit_code.description: The exit codes a floor result can carry. A closed set.

code.description: What kind of warning it is. An open set: a later release may add a code, and a script ignores one it does not know. file_error says a file could not be read.

warning.description: One warning. Its sentence is also in summary.

field.description: The header field that may differ.

override.description: One blocking field a --override flag let differ.
